To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of large multi-touch displays in public space is highly socially organized, with many people interacting with the system in parallel.

1) the public display was used by a diverse group of people in many different social configurations; 2) the use of the display was organized in a way that was different from the way it was organized in private settings; 3) this was achieved through social negotiation and learning; 4) the display was used for social interaction as well as for information seeking and entertainment; 5) the display restructured the public space in which it was installed.
Public multi-touch displays are used as a stage, a meeting place and an arena of conflict and negotiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social organization of public use, and the design of public displays in particular.
the design of technology for public spaces, and we believe that the design of technology must be informed by a better understanding of how people use public spaces.

the social aspects of multi-user public interaction, the social aspects of large multi-touch displays, the social aspects in the public use of interactive public spaces, and the social aspects of public displays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CityWall system was a successful and engaging public display.
public displays are social objects that can be appropriated by users in many different ways.

the public display is a social object that is appropriated by users in various ways, and that the appropriation process is an ongoing, dynamic, and complex process that is affected both by the physical properties of the system, as well as by the social and cultural environment of its use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of public display is a social practice.
the CityWall is a public space that is not a space.
the public use of a multi-touch display is not just a scaled-up version of its domestic use, but that it is shaped by the public setting, the display size, and the multi-touch feature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
public displays can be used as a platform for social interaction and communication, but the design must support the social practices that are used in these situations.
the design of a public multi-touch display needs to consider how it is used in a public space and the ways in which it changes the space.
public displays are not just for public information.
